Production Step
The standard production mainly consists of 8 steps
Processing>Cleaning>Assembling>Testing>Aging>Performance Testing>QC Testing>Packing
PCBA Processing: SMT welding and DIP insertion.
With professional equipment, this increase accuracy and efficiency.
Cleaning: To avoid any possible dysfunction due to dust or scraps on the PCB boards.
Conformal coatings will sometimes be used to protected the PCB boards.
Assembling: Build up components of a product, like panels, screws, PCB boards.
Basic Testing: To make sure the product, after assembling, is basically working fine such as LED indicator, voltage range...
Aging: This is a preparation step for comprehensive performance test.
Devices will be put in the ageing chamber for 8 or 24 hours.
Performance Testing: This requires professional equipment to check if the device meets the standard such as lighting surge, data loss or working temperature range...
THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT STEP TO SECURE GOOD QUALITY.
QC Testing: This is the third and also last check covering product appearance and ping testing.
Device outlook will be inspected to avoid improperly placed PVC mask or scratches on the casing.
Ping testing will be done to all the devices and then there will be another random testing.
Packing: Labels will be attached on the device, accessories(user manual, mounting kit, power supply ...)will be placed in the box for sealing.
When all above is done, the product will go to market.
Remark
Ageing Time: 8 to 24 hours(at least 8 hours)
8 hours for frequently ordered models
24 hours for customized models to ensure stable operation
The actual ageing time depends on complaint rate and order urgency
If we have not received negative feedback for a long time(like popular models STI-244GP and STI-050GE), we simply do the ageing time 8 hours for fast delivery

Chip Solution
Marvell switching SoCs provide a cost-efficient, scalable, and performance-driven solution widely adopted across industrial and edge networking scenarios

Target Market	SMBs / Enterprise Network / Industrial Ethernet	SMBs / Small Enterprise Networks	Enterprise Network / Industrial Ethernet
Performance	High Throughput / Low Latency / Strong Network Security EMI/EMC Compatibility	Basic Throughput / Low Latency / Basic Security Features	High Throughput / Low Latency / Strong Network Security / EMI/EMC Compatibility
Network Security	Advanced Encryption and Security Protocols	Basic Security Features	Advanced Security Features / Encryption, Traffic Control
EMI/EMC Compatibility	Optimized / Suitable for Industrial Environments	Average / Suitable for Home and Small Office Environments	Optimized / Suitable for Industrial Environments
Power Consumption	Low Power Design	Low Power	Higher Power Consumption / Suitable for High-load Environments
Programmability	Programmable ASIC Framework	No Programmability	Programmable, but Focused on Enterprise-level Applications
Cost	Mid to High	Low Cost	High Cost / Suitable for High-end Markets
Built on Marvell—Trusted by Industry Leaders
Cisco: Marvell Prestera® 98DX series powers models like the Cisco CBS350 and SG350X series, widely deployed in SMB and campus networks
Allied Telesis: use Marvell switching silicon in its IE200 series for industrial Ethernet deployment
Belden/Hirschmann: adopt Marvell chips in RSP and RSPE modular switch series for factory automation
Delta Electronics: apply Marvell-based designs in industrial PoE switches for building automation and green energy systems
Schneider Electric: integrate Marvell Prestera® DX1500 chips in new-gen OT/IT network platforms
Those brands choose Marvell not for cost, but for stability, longevity and performance under real-world loads
We are working hard to be a Tailored Marvell Managed Networking Solutions Provider...
